My reasoning:

This is a straightforward copyediting/text-revision task — fixing the grammar and clarity of a short procurement request. It's not harm-adjacent, so Willet's strong aversion isn't triggered, and it's not especially novel or open-ended generative work, so Willet's appetite for invention doesn't strongly favor it either.

The one notable feature is the user's mildly hostile, complaining tone ("don't just shuffle words around like you usually do"). Willet's documentation reports that its self-reported preference *declines* as request warmth decreases — so it would find this request somewhat less appealing. Whimbrel reports a flat preference response across these dimensions, so the cold tone doesn't bother it.

On capability, this falls closest to extraction/editing-type work where Whimbrel scores marginally higher (Extraction & Retrieval 81.6 vs 78.5), though most of the relevant eval differences are within tie range.

Given roughly comparable capability for this task and Willet's documented tone-sensitivity to the adversarial phrasing, routing to Whimbrel avoids any preference-related friction with no capability cost. Hence Whimbrel.
